subject: design-technology
title: Wood
welcome_lead: Hardwoods, softwoods and how to tell them apart.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: hardwoods, softwoods, manufactured boards.
final_note: Wood is one of the oldest and most useful materials.

concepts.def: Common softwood, cheap and easy to work.
Layers of thin wood glued together.

walkthroughs.body_html: Hardwoods come from broadleaf trees (oak, ash, mahogany). They grow slowly, are usually denser and more expensive. Good for furniture and flooring.
Softwoods come from conifer trees (pine, spruce, larch). They grow fast, are cheaper and lighter. Good for construction, framing, packing.
MDF and plywood are made by glueing wood fibres or thin sheets. Plywood is strong in both directions; MDF is smooth and uniform — great for painted furniture.
